lines.say: Calculus, visually. Chapter one: the derivative.

lines.text: A car pulls away. After $t$ seconds it has gone [[f|$t^2$ metres]].
lines.say: A car pulls away. After t seconds, it's gone t squared metres.

lines.text: Its speed keeps changing. What does the speedometer say at exactly $t = 1$?
lines.say: Its speed keeps changing. What does the speedometer say at exactly one second?

lines.text: Average speed is easy: distance ÷ time, the [[w|slope of this line]].
lines.say: Average speed is easy: distance over time. The slope of this line.

lines.text: From $t = 1$ to $t = 3$: 8 m in 2 s, an average of 4 m/s.
lines.say: From one second to three: eight metres in two seconds. Four metres per second.

lines.text: Now shrink the interval. Let the second moment, $t = 1 + h$, slide toward the first.
lines.say: Now shrink the interval. Let the second moment, one plus h, slide toward the first.

lines.text: The slope settles on one number, 2. The line stops cutting the curve and just [[d|touches]] it.
lines.say: The slope settles on a single number: two. The line stops cutting through the curve, and just touches it.

lines.text: The algebra agrees. Expand the square, and the 1s cancel…
lines.say: The algebra agrees. Expand the square, and the ones cancel.

lines.text: …leaving $2 + h$. As $h$ shrinks to nothing, only 2 is left: [[d|2 m/s at $t = 1$]].
lines.say: That leaves two plus h. As h shrinks to nothing, only two is left. Two metres per second.

lines.text: Do this at every instant and you get a new function: the [[d|derivative]].
lines.say: Do this at every instant, and you get a new function: the derivative.

lines.text: For $s(t) = t^2$, the slope at time $t$ is always [[d|$2t$]]. That is the speedometer reading.
lines.say: For t squared, the slope at time t is always two t. That's the speedometer reading.
The derivative: rise over run, as the run shrinks to zero.
